cross_source_qualifications.role: Both relevant date claims are user assertions. Assistant echoes/advice are not independent evidence of purchase or delivery.
cross_source_qualifications.event_and_referent: In each user turn, “it” refers locally to a backpack. Across two distinct sessions the work-laptop use and new-backpack language make the same-item link plausible, but no durable item ID explicitly certifies identity.
cross_source_qualifications.time: Turn observations are Jan 24, 2023, both before the as-of cutoff. The event dates are written as 1/15 and 1/20 without explicit year; 2023 follows from Jan 24 turn context, so preserve that inference rather than labeling the year as quoted.
cross_source_qualifications.quantity: The two proposed date phrases are the purchase and arrival operands for an elapsed-days question. This review does not compute or certify a corrected answer.
cross_source_qualifications.modality: Both relevant dates are retrospective user reports (“bought”, “arrived”), not plans. Other proposals contain conditional advice or unrelated future-dated claims.
cross_source_qualifications.correction_and_negation: The bounded lexical scan found no other eligible backpack purchase or arrival date claim that contradicts these two turns; this is not proof no paraphrased correction exists elsewhere.
cross_source_qualifications.new_information: Both relevant original turns already occur exactly once in the legacy baseline, including their date clauses; all six other proposed original turns also occur exactly once and add no relevant backpack event.

limitations: Legacy baseline is mixed evidence and not ground truth.
